claims.text: Increasing compensating Hf content in Nb-, Ta-, Ti-, or Zr-containing refractory high-entropy alloys produces specific local lattice distortions.
Hf-induced local lattice distortions promote short-range order.
The resulting short-range order stabilizes dislocation dynamics.
The Hf-driven structural changes reduce thermal expansion at high temperatures.
Baseline refractory high-entropy alloys lacking compensatory Hf exhibit inherent lattice mismatches.
The Hf-free baseline has a higher thermal-expansion coefficient than the proposed Hf-modified alloy.
Hf can be introduced incrementally while reducing one or more of Nb, Ta, Ti, or Zr to maintain overall composition balance.
Compensatory Hf modulates dislocation nucleation and mobility.
Compensatory Hf reduces local lattice strain and lattice mismatch.
Reduced local strain and mismatch lead to a more homogeneous distribution of dislocations.
A more homogeneous dislocation distribution increases tensile strength.
A more homogeneous dislocation distribution improves thermoelastic behavior by mitigating excess thermal expansion.
Hf-induced structural changes stabilize the microstructure against high-temperature distortions.
An optimized Hf content will produce higher tensile strength than the Hf-free baseline.
An optimized Hf content will produce a lower or more stable thermal-expansion coefficient than the Hf-free baseline.
The proposed mechanism is primarily applicable at service temperatures above 1000°C.
Molecular-dynamics simulations may not capture all long-range phenomena relevant to the proposed behavior.
Failure to observe both improved tensile strength and reduced or better-controlled thermal expansion in Hf-compensated alloys would falsify the predicted performance.
Absence of a correlation between Hf-induced local lattice distortions and dislocation behavior would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and structural-mediator fields say Hf induces local lattice distortions, whereas the mechanism says Hf reduces local lattice strain and mismatch. These could be compatible if Hf creates particular local distortions that relieve net mismatch, but that distinction is not stated.
